description:
Redwood Inference is standardizing how it models and exposes inference cost so that Console (cost breakdown + transparency) and Optimize (recommendations for batching/caching/quantization profiles) can operate on consistent, auditable economics across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments.

Goals:
- Define a “Standard Cost Model” (SCM) spec: canonical inputs, outputs, units, and semantics for estimating and attributing inference cost.
- Ship a versioned Cost Model API that can be called by Console and Optimize services (and optionally internal tooling) with deterministic results.
- Align runtime telemetry (token-level metering, batching/caching signals, quantization profile metadata) with the SCM so attribution is explainable and comparable across regions/hardware.
- Provide guardrails: backward compatibility policy, validation rules, audit logging, and SLOs.

Scope:
- Spec work: cost model taxonomy (compute, memory, cache hits, batch efficiency), required/optional inputs, normalization across hardware SKUs, and output schema (total cost + breakdown + confidence/assumptions).
- API work: endpoints for “estimate” and “explain/attribution”, version negotiation, and integration into Console cost pages and Optimize recommendation pipelines.
- Data plumbing: runtime emits the signals needed by the model (batch size effective, KV-cache hit rate, prefill/decode split, quant profile id, region/SKU), telemetry pipelines preserve dimensionality with cardinality controls.
- Rollout: feature flags, canary, dashboards/alerts, and documentation.

Non-goals (initial release):
- Direct customer-facing billing changes (SCM outputs must not become the source of truth for invoices until explicitly approved).
- A full pricing engine (discounts/contract terms remain separate); SCM focuses on technical cost attribution and consistent estimates.

Key stakeholders:
- Product: Aditya Rao (Optimize), Marissa Cole (Console & Rollouts), Nikhil Sharma / Henry Cho (Hosted API ergonomics).
- Engineering Platform/Control Plane: Priya Natarajan, Ethan Park, Benji Okafor, Jordan Lee.
- Console & Tooling: Dylan Brooks, Chloe Martin, Jada Williams.
- Telemetry: Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman.
- Serving Runtime & Applied ML: Mateo Alvarez, Sofia Ivanova, Dr. Maya Srinivasan, Arjun Desai, Hassan Mirza.
- SRE/Infra: Neha Kapoor, Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes.
- Security/Compliance (review): audit logging + access controls for sensitive customer cost data.

Phases / timeline (typical ~8–10 weeks):
1) Discovery + alignment: define use-cases (Console breakdown, Optimize what-if), gather telemetry gaps, agree on nomenclature and units.
2) Spec + ADRs: schema, versioning strategy, deterministic calculation requirements, and boundary between “estimate” vs “metered attribution”.
3) Implementation: Cost Model service + library, runtime instrumentation hooks, telemetry pipeline updates, and API gateway integration.
4) Integrations: Console cost breakdown page wiring; Optimize recommendation pipeline consuming SCM outputs.
5) Launch: staged rollout by tenant/tier, dashboards and alerts, documentation, and post-launch retro.

Constraints:
- Must be stable across deployments and regions (same inputs => same outputs).
- Must be resilient to missing signals (explicit assumptions/confidence fields, strict validation).
- Must control metric cardinality and PII/customer-sensitive exposure; audit logs for reads of customer-level cost breakdowns.

files.description: PRD for the Standard Cost Model spec + API: target users (Console/Optimize), problem statement, success metrics (accuracy bands, latency, adoption), milestones, and rollout plan.
Formal SCM v1 spec: definitions, required inputs, output schema (total + breakdown), units, examples for common workloads, and explicit assumptions/confidence semantics.
API standards for the Cost Model API: versioning strategy, error model, idempotency, pagination (if needed), and compatibility commitments for Console/Optimize clients.
ADR choosing schema versioning + negotiation approach (header vs path vs payload), plus migration strategy for future cost components (e.g., new cache types, new GPU SKUs).
Service architecture doc: ownership, dependencies (telemetry, model catalog, pricing tables), data flow, caching, and deployment topology across regions.
How-to for Console engineers: calling patterns, recommended client timeouts/retries, interpreting breakdown fields, and safe fallback behavior when the API is unavailable.
How-to for Optimize: ‘what-if’ evaluation inputs (batching/caching/quant profile candidates), running scenario sweeps, and guarding against misleading recommendations.
Runtime instrumentation requirements: which counters/timers are emitted (prefill/decode split, batch efficiency, KV-cache hit rates), tagging rules, and performance overhead limits.
Guidelines linking quantization profiles to cost attribution: profile identifiers, expected compute/memory deltas, validation methodology, and known edge cases.
SLO doc for Cost Model API: availability, p95/p99 latency targets, error budget policy, and alert thresholds tied to Console/Optimize dependency criticality.
Audit logging spec for cost-model reads: event fields, retention, sensitive fields redaction, and integration with existing audit pipelines.
Early working draft: terminology debates, open questions (metered vs estimated), and rough schema sketches with annotated examples.
Spreadsheet-style doc listing candidate metrics/dimensions for cost attribution, with cardinality estimates and proposed aggregation strategy.
Console integration notes: which SCM fields map to UI sections, copy/UX considerations for ‘assumptions’, and mock payloads used for development.
Experiment log for quantization profiles: measured deltas vs SCM estimates, anomalies by model family, and follow-up tasks for profile metadata.
PM working doc: Optimize user stories requiring SCM, scenario templates (batching on/off, cache warm/cold, quant profile swap), and acceptance criteria.
Risk assessment for launch: dependency mapping, failure modes, fallback behaviors in Console/Optimize, and canary gating criteria.
Release checklist: migrations, config toggles, dashboards readiness, smoke tests, and comms templates for staged rollout.
PM ticket tracking PRD completion and cross-functional sign-off; includes success metrics, milestones, and dependency list.

Telemetry ticket: add/standardize dimensions needed by SCM, implement cardinality controls, and ensure data availability to Cost Model service.
